topic: How bow speed and pressure create an expressive tone just before violin-string vibration becomes unstable
title: The Bow's Narrow Zone of Expressive Tone
hook: How can a violin bow shape musical expression?
description: Two independent string-music publications describe a computer model that tested one hundred bow–string interaction points. The reported result: expressive tone peaked close to the point where the string's regular vibration became unstable.
cover_payoff: Use the generated solo-violin audio bed as a symbolic listening payoff while animated lines show a stable waveform approaching instability. No real creator performance recording is included, so do not call it Prince's live performance.
narration_script: How can a violin bow shape musical expression? A detailed model tested one hundred bow and string interaction points. It found expressivity peaked just before the waveform became unstable. That useful sound zone was narrow, balancing expressive tone with careful control.

narration_evidence.quote: used the programming language Python to simulate a violin string, and then modelled the interaction between bow and string, investigating how changes in bow speed and pressure affect the resulting sound.
He found that expressivity was highest at the moment right before the waveform became unstable
there is a small zone in pressure and speed where the sound is most expressive before it becomes unstable.
